agent_note: Prose fiction, not verse -- the lyric density is high and several quotes are verbless fragments, but the surrounding material is clearly narrative prose. First-person adult narrator looking back on adolescence, so the reflective register that would be gnomic in a present-tense novel is here almost all cast in PAST tense ('That was part of being a girl -- you were resigned to...'). Those quotes stay event/past per the present-tense-only gnomic rule and are flagged in notes; they are the audit-sensitive set for this book. No dialogue quotes at all.
